messages:
dana: quick follow-up to the service-auth RFC — thinking we should minimize the exposed service key surface. proposal: keep one org-scoped long-lived key per runtime, and mint short-lived project-scoped tokens for resource access. short thread to call out tradeoffs.

maya: can you sketch the minting flow? e.g. how a service running in project X gets a token to call a project-scoped API?

dana: flow sketch: org-key stored in KMS on runtime nodes. when svc needs project access, it calls local mint endpoint: POST /mint {target_project: "p-123", scopes: ["read.buckets"]} -> returns JWT with proj claim + exp=5m, aud=target-api. minting audited.

leo: main worry: org-scoped key leakage. that single key can mint tokens for any project. blast radius seems larger than per-project keys.

dana: agreed. mitigations: 1) org-key never leaves KMS hardware, only used by runtime processes. 2) mint endpoint requires runtime identity + attestation. 3) mint rate limits + anomaly alerts. 4) keep minted tokens short (1-5m).

sam: audit needs: minted token id, issuer runtime id, target_project, scopes, trace_id. we should be able to show "svc X minted token T for proj p-123 at t" in logs. also immutable token id so we can revoke if needed.

maya: SDK changes: provide helper mintToken(project, scopes) which calls local mint endpoint and refreshes. fallback: host a proxy that mints for older runtimes. also surface metrics for mint latency and failure rates.

leo: rotation question — how often rotate org-key? daily seems heavy. ops cost and rollout complexity. maybe rotate monthly but be able to revoke mint capability instantly if compromised.

dana: plan: rotate key material quarterly by default, with an ops kill-switch to flip a "disable-minting" flag per runtime. KMS supports key versioning so runtime can switch without redeploy.

sam: RBAC mapping: do we map project claim -> role checks, or rely solely on token scopes?

maya: both. token scopes are coarse (read/write etc). resource-level RBAC still checks project claim + an authorization table (svc-role for project). allows fine-grained controls without per-project key churn.

auth-bot: NOTE: new /mint endpoint will emit structured audit events: {event: "mint", issuer: "runtime-42", target_project: "p-123", scopes: ["read.buckets"], token_id: "t-abc", ts: 1722223333}. Ops alert threshold: >100 tokens/min per runtime.

leo: how about offline jobs? they can't call local mint. do we allow short-lived delegated credentials via a signing service?

dana: Offline flow: an admin can request a delegated token with embedded usage policy and TTL via a signed request. This is separate and audited heavily. Prefer orchestrated ephemeral jobs over static per-project keys.

maya: also need backward compatibility path: existing per-project keys should continue to work while we roll out minting. migration plan: phase 1 minting opt-in, phase 2 recommend SDK change, phase 3 deprecate old keys after N months.

sam: logging schema I'll draft: fields + example queries for Sumo/Logsight so security can prove which project was affected.

leo: checklist for RFC follow-up: 1) token format spec (claims + alg) 2) mint endpoint auth + attestation 3) audit event schema 4) SDK helpers + fallback proxy 5) revoke/ops kill-switch 6) rollout timeline + compat plan.

dana: great. i'll draft the follow-up RFC with that checklist. @maya will you take SDK ownership? @sam can you own audit schema?

maya: yup, i'll own SDK helpers and the proxy fallback. ETA EOW.

sam: I'll write the audit fields and example queries this week.

dana: thanks. if anyone sees a security hole in the flow call it out here or ping me directly.

leo: :+1:

maya: :raised_hands:
